description: NaBa₄Ga₂B₈(O₆Br)₃ crystallizes in the tetragonal P4₂nm space group. Na is bonded to four equivalent O and one Br atom to form distorted NaBrO₄ square pyramids that share edges with two equivalent BO₄ tetrahedra. All Na-O bond lengths are 2.61 Å. The Na-Br bond length is 2.98 Å. Ba is bonded in a 10-coordinate geometry to seven O and three Br atoms. There are a spread of Ba-O bond distances ranging from 2.83-3.35 Å. There are a spread of Ba-Br bond distances ranging from 3.24-3.44 Å. Ga is bonded to four O atoms to form GaO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two BO₄ tetrahedra. All Ga-O bond lengths are 1.86 Å. There are three inequivalent B sites. In the first B site, B is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to three O atoms. There is one shorter (1.37 Å) and two longer (1.39 Å) B-O bond lengths. In the second B site, B is bonded to four O atoms to form BO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one GaO₄ tetrahedra and  a cornercorner with one BO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of B-O bond distances ranging from 1.45-1.50 Å. In the third B site, B is bonded to four O atoms to form BO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one GaO₄ tetrahedra,  a cornercorner with one BO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaBrO₄ square pyramid. There are a spread of B-O bond distances ranging from 1.45-1.54 Å. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Ba, one Ga, and one B atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted water-like geometry to two equivalent Ba and two B atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent Ba and two B atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na, one Ba, and two B atoms. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent Ba, one Ga, and one B atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent Ba, one Ga, and one B atom. There are two inequivalent Br sites. In the first Br site, Br is bonded to four equivalent Ba atoms to form BrBa₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent BrBa₄Na square pyramids and edges with two equivalent BrBa₄ tetrahedra. In the second Br site, Br is bonded to one Na and four equivalent Ba atoms to form distorted corner-sharing BrBa₄Na square pyramids.
